chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a woman who became ill during the month of Ramadan, or menstruated, or traveled, then died before the month of Ramadan ended. Should it be made up on her behalf?
He said: 'As for menstruation and illness, no. But as for travel, yes.'

key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan in which fasting is obligatory
key_terms.يُقْضَى: it is made up or performed as qaḍāʾ on behalf of someone

ai.seo_question: Should missed Ramadan fasts be made up for a woman who dies during the month after illness, menstruation, or travel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about making up missed fasts on behalf of a woman who dies during Ramadan before the month ends. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between missed fasting due to menstruation or illness, for which no make-up is due on her behalf, and missed fasting due to travel, for which it is due.
